Main.sentence: The 2014 Winter Olympics , officially called the XXII Olympic Winter Games ( ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ : XXII Олимпийские зимние игры , romanised: XXII Olimpiyskiye zimniye igry ) and commonly known as Sochi 2014 ( ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ : Сочи 2014 ), were an international winter ___E:multi-sport event U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-sport_event)___ that was held from 7 to 23 February 2014 in ___E:Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi)___ , Russia.
Opening rounds in certain events were held on 6 February 2014, the day before the ___E:opening ceremony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics_opening_ceremony)___ .

These were the first Olympic Games under the ___E:International Olympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee)___ (IOC) presidency of ___E:Thomas Bach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Bach)___ .

Both the Olympics and ___E:Paralympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Paralympics)___ were organised by the ___E:Sochi Organizing Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_2014_Olympic_and_Paralympic_Organizing_Committee)___ (SOOC).

Sochi was selected as the host city on 5 July 2007, during the 119th ___E:IOC Session U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_IOC_meetings#IOC_Sessions)___ held in ___E:Guatemala City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_City)___ .

It was the first Olympics to be held in a ___E:CIS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States)___ state and former ___E:Warsaw Pact U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact)___ state after the ___E:Revolutions of 1989 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989)___ and the ___E:collapse of the Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union)___ in 1991. The ___E:Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ previously hosted the Summer Olympics in ___E:1980 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics)___ .
A record ninety-eight events in fifteen winter sport disciplines were held during the Games.

A number of new competitions—a total of twelve accounting for gender—were held during the Games, including ___E:biathlon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biathlon)___ mixed relay, women's ___E:ski jumping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ski_jumping)___ , mixed-team ___E:figure skating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figure_skating)___ , mixed-team ___E:luge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luge)___ , ___E:half-pipe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-pipe)___ skiing, ski and snowboard ___E:slopestyle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slopestyle)___ , and snowboard ___E:parallel slalom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_slalom)___ .

The events were held around two clusters of new venues: an Olympic Park constructed in Sochi's ___E:Imeretinsky Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imeretinsky_Valley)___ on the coast of the ___E:Black Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea)___ , with ___E:Fisht Olympic Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisht_Olympic_Stadium)___ , and the Games' indoor venues located within walking distance; and snow events in the ___E:resort settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort_town)___ of ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ .
The 2014 Winter Olympics were the most ___E:expensive Games U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost_of_the_Olympic_Games)___ in the history of the Olympics.

While originally budgeted at ___E:US$ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US$)___ 12 billion, major cost overruns caused this figure to expand to US$51 billion, more than three times the cost of the ___E:2012 London Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics)___ and even surpassing the estimated cost of US$44 billion for the ___E:2008 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)___ in Beijing.
The 2014 Games achieved a record broadcast audience of 2.1 billion people worldwide.

In 2016, an ___E:independent report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Report)___ commissioned by the ___E:World Anti-Doping Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Anti-Doping_Agency)___ confirmed allegations that the Russian Olympic team had been involved in a ___E:state-sponsored doping program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia)___ , active from at least late 2011 through August 2015. The program was active during the Winter Olympics in Sochi, and athletes had benefited from the ___E:cover-up U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover-up)___ .

The IOC stripped thirteen medals from Russian athletes in 2017, but nine were reinstated by the ___E:Court of Arbitration for Sport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport)___ .

In December 2017, the IOC voted to suspend the ___E:Russian Olympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Olympic_Committee)___ , with an option for ___E:whitelisted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitelist)___ athletes to compete ___E:independently U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics)___ during the ___E:2018 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics)___ .

Sochi was elected on 4 July 2007 during the 119th ___E:International Olympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee)___ (IOC) session held in ___E:Guatemala City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala_City)___ , ___E:Guatemala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala)___ , defeating bids from ___E:Salzburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salzburg)___ , ___E:Austria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria)___ ; and ___E:Pyeongchang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyeongchang_County)___ , South Korea.
This is the first time that the ___E:Russian Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ has hosted the Winter Olympics.

The ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union_at_the_1980_Summer_Olympics)___ was the host of the ___E:1980 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics)___ held in and around Moscow.
As of October 2013, the estimated combined cost of the 2014 Winter Olympics had topped US$51 billion.
This amount included the cost for Olympic games themselves and cost of Sochi infrastructural projects (roads, railroads, power plants).

This total is over four times the initial budget of $12 billion (compared to the $8 billion spent for the ___E:2010 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics)___ in Vancouver), and made the Sochi games the most expensive Olympics in history, exceeding the estimated $44 billion cost of the ___E:2008 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)___ in Beijing,  which hosted 3 times as many events.  ___E:Dmitry Kozak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitry_Kozak)___ was the main overseer for the events in Sochi.

In its final budget published in June 2014, Olimpstroy—the state corporation that oversaw the Sochi Olympics development—reported the total allocated funds for the 2014 Sochi Winter Olympics of 1,524 billion rubles (US$49.5 billion).

However, only about a fifth of that budget ($10.8 billion) was directly related to the Olympic games, while the rest went into urban and regional regeneration and the conversion of the Sochi region into an all-year round sea and alpine resort.
The breakdown table below is based on a report that has analyzed the distribution of Olimpstroy's $49.5 billion budget.
Estimates also suggest that additional unrecoverable operational costs (including for security) could have added another $3 billion.

With an average February temperature of 8.3 °C (46.9 °F) and a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___ , Sochi is the warmest city to host a Winter Olympic Games.
Sochi 2014 is the 12th straight Olympics to outlaw smoking; all Sochi venues, Olympic Park bars and restaurants and public areas were smoke-free during the Games.
It is also the first time that an Olympic Park has been built for hosting winter games. [citation needed]

The Sochi Olympic Park was built by the ___E:Black Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea)___ coast in the ___E:Imeretinsky Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imeretinsky_Valley)___ , about 4 km (2.5 miles) from Russia's ___E:border U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia%E2%80%93Russia_border)___ with ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abkhazia)___ / ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(country))___ .
The venues were clustered around a central water basin on which the Medals Plaza is built, allowing all indoor venues to be within walking distance.

It also features "The Waters of the Olympic Park" (designed by ___E:California U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California)___ -based company ___E:WET U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WET_(company))___ ), a choreographed fountain which served as the backdrop in the medals awards and the opening and closing ceremonies of the event.
The new venues include:

A ___E:street circuit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street_circuit)___ known as the ___E:Sochi Autodrom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_Autodrom)___ was constructed in and around Olympic Park. Its primary use is to host the ___E:Formula One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One)___ ___E:Russian Grand Prix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Grand_Prix)___ , which held its ___E:inaugural edition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Russian_Grand_Prix)___ in October 2014.

In January 2015, work began on adapting Fisht Olympic Stadium into an open-air football stadium to host matches during the ___E:2018 FIFA World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup)___ .

A new ice hockey team in the ___E:Kontinental Hockey League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinental_Hockey_League)___ , ___E:HC Sochi Leopards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HC_Sochi)___ , now plays in Bolshoy Arena.
The Olympic infrastructure was constructed according to a Federal Target Program (FTP).
In June 2009, the Games' organisers reported they were one year ahead in building the main Olympic facilities as compared to recent Olympic Games.

In November 2011, ___E:IOC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOC)___ President ___E:Jacques Rogge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Rogge)___ was in Sochi and concluded that the city had made significant progress since he last visited eighteen months earlier.

According to the FTP, US$580 million would be spent on construction and modernisation of telecommunications in the region. ___E:Avaya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avaya)___ was named by the Sochi Organizing Committee as the official supplier of telecommunications equipment.

Avaya provided the data network equipment, including ___E:switches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switch)___ , ___E:routers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Router_(computing))___ , security, telephones and ___E:contact-centre systems U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_centre)___ .
It provided engineers and technicians to design and test the systems, and worked with other technology partners to provide athletes, dignitaries and fans information about the Games.
The 2014 Olympics is the first "fabric-enabled" Games using ___E:Shortest Path Bridging U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortest_Path_Bridging)___ (SPB) technology.
The network is capable of handling up to 54 Tbit/s of traffic.
Infrastructure built for the games included:

During the Games, the ___E:core networks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_network)___ of ___E:Rostelecom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rostelecom)___ and ___E:Transtelekom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transtelekom)___ were used.
In January 2012, the newest equipment for the television coverage of the Games arrived in the port of ___E:Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_Microdistrict)___ .
Prepared specifically for the Games, a team of regional specialists and the latest technology provide a qualitatively new level of television production in the region.
The fibre-optic channel links Sochi between ___E:Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlersky_City_District)___ and Krasnaya Polyana.
The 46-kilometre-long (29 mi) channel enables videoconferencing and news reporting from the Olympics.

In November 2013, it was reported that the fibre-optic cable that was built by the ___E:Federal Communications Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Federal_Communications_Agency)___ , Rossvyaz, had no operator.

With Rostelecom and Megafon both refusing to operate it, the line was transferred to the ownership of the state enterprise Center for Monitoring & Development of Infocommunication Technologies (Russian: Центр МИР ИТ ).
Russian mobile phone operator ___E:Megafon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megafon)___ expanded and improved Sochi's telecom infrastructure with over 700 new 2G/3G/4G cell towers.
Sochi was the first Games to offer ___E:4G connectivity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_term_evolution)___ at a speed of 10 MB/sec.

In January 2014, Rostelecom reported that it had connected the Olympic media centre in Sochi to the Internet and organised channels of communication with the main media centre of the Olympic Games in the coastal cluster and press centre in Moscow.
The media centre was built at total cost of 17 million rubles.

A five-year strategy for increasing the power supply of the Sochi region was presented by Russian energy experts during a seminar on 29 May 2009, held by the Sochi 2014 Organizing Committee, and attended by International Olympic Committee (IOC) experts and officials from the ___E:Russian Ministry of Regional Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Ministry_of_Regional_Development)___ , the ___E:Russian Ministry of Energy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Ministry_of_Energy)___ , the State Corporation Olimpstroy and the Krasnodar Krai administration.
According to the strategy, the capacity of the regional energy network would increase by two and a half times by 2014, guaranteeing a stable power supply during and after the Games.
The power demand of Sochi at the end of May 2009 was 424 MW. The power demand of the Olympic infrastructure was expected to be about 340 MW.

Earlier plans also include building ___E:combined cycle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_cycle)___ (steam and gas) power stations near the cities of ___E:Tuapse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuapse)___ and ___E:Novorossiysk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novorossiysk)___ and construction of a cable-wire powerline, partially on the floor of the ___E:Black Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea)___ .
The transport infrastructure prepared to support the Olympics includes many roads, tunnels, bridges, interchanges, railroads and stations in and around Sochi.
Among others, 8 flyovers, 102 bridges, tens of tunnels and a bypass route for heavy trucks – 367 km (228 mi) of roads were paved.

The ___E:Sochi Light Metro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_Light_Metro)___ is located between ___E:Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlersky_City_District)___ and ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ connecting the Olympic Park, ___E:Sochi International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_International_Airport)___ , and the venues in Krasnaya Polyana.

The existing 102 km (63-mile), Tuapse-to-Adler railroad was renovated to provide double track throughout, increasing capacity and enabling a reliable regional service to be provided and extending to the airport.

In December 2009, ___E:Russian Railways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Railways)___ ordered 38 ___E:Siemens Mobility U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens_Mobility)___ ___E:Desiro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens_Desiro)___ trains for delivery in 2013 for use during the Olympics, with an option for a further 16 partly built in Russia.

At ___E:Sochi International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_International_Airport)___ , a new terminal was built along a 3.5 km (2.2-mile) ___E:runway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runway)___ extension, overlapping the ___E:Mzymta River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mzymta_River)___ .

At the ___E:Port of Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Sochi)___ , a new offshore terminal 1.5 km (0.93 mi) from the shore allows docking for cruise ships with capacities of 3,000 passengers.
The cargo terminal of the seaport would be moved from the centre of Sochi.
Roadways were detoured, some going around the construction site and others being cut off.

In May 2009, Russian Railways started the construction of tunnel complex No. 1 (the final total is six) on the combined road (automobile and railway) from Adler to Alpica Service Mountain Resort in the Krasnaya Polyana region.
The tunnel complex No. 1 is located near Akhshtyr in Adlersky City District, and includes:
Russian Railways president ___E:Vladimir Yakunin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Yakunin)___ stated the road construction costed more than 200 billion rubles.
In addition, Sochi's railway stations were renovated.

These are ___E:Dagomys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagomys_railway_station)___ , ___E:Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_railway_station)___ , ___E:Matsesta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsesta_railway_station)___ , ___E:Khosta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosta_railway_station)___ , ___E:Lazarevskaya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevskaya_railway_station)___ , and ___E:Loo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loo_railway_station)___ railway stations.

In Adler, a ___E:new railway station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_railway_station)___ was built while the original building was preserved, and in the Olympic park cluster, a new station was built from scratch, the ___E:Olympic Park railway station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Park_railway_station,_Sochi)___ .
Another ___E:new railway station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana_railway_station)___ was built in Estosadok, close to Krasnaya Polyana.
Funds were spent on the construction of hotels for 10,300 guests.

The first of the Olympic hotels, Zvezdny ( Stellar ), was rebuilt anew.  Significant funds were spent on the construction of an advanced ___E:sewage treatment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sewage_treatment)___ system in Sochi, designed by Olimpstroy.

The system meets BREF standards and employs top available technologies for environment protection, including ___E:tertiary treatment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_treatment)___ with ___E:microfiltration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microfiltration)___ .

Six ___E:post offices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_office)___ were opened at competition venues, two of them in the main media centre in Olympic Park and in the mountain village of ___E:Estosadok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estosadok)___ .
In addition to standard services, customers had access to unique services including two new products, Fotomarka and Retropismo.
Fotomarka presents an opportunity to get a stylised sheet of eight souvenir stamps with one's own photos, using the services of a photographer in the office.
Retropismo service allows a customer to write with their own stylus or pen on antique paper with further letters, winding string and wax seal affixing.
All the new sites and post offices in Sochi were opened during the Olympics until late night 7 days a week, and employees were trained to speak English.

On 29 September 2013, the Olympic torch was lit in ___E:Ancient Olympia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Olympia)___ , beginning a seven-day journey across Greece and on to Russia, then the ___E:torch relay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_torch_relays)___ started at Moscow on 7 October 2013 before passing 83 Russian cities and arriving at Sochi on the day of the opening ceremony, 7 February 2014.  It is the longest torch relay in Olympic history, a 60,000-kilometre (40,000-mile) route that passes through all regions of the country, from ___E:Kaliningrad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaliningrad)___ in the west to ___E:Chukotka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chukotka_Autonomous_Okrug)___ in the east.

The Olympic torch reached the ___E:North Pole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Pole)___ for first time via a ___E:nuclear-powered icebreaker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear-powered_icebreaker)___ (50 Let Pobedy) .

The torch was also passed for the first time in ___E:space U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_space)___ , though not lit for the duration of the flight for safety reasons, on flight ___E:Soyuz TMA-11M U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-11M)___ to the ___E:International Space Station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station)___ (ISS).
The spacecraft itself was adorned with Olympic-themed ___E:livery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livery)___ including the Games' emblem.

Russian ___E:cosmonauts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmonaut)___ ___E:Oleg Kotov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Kotov)___ and ___E:Sergey Ryazansky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergey_Ryazansky)___ waved the torch on a spacewalk outside the ISS. The torch returned to Earth five days later on board ___E:Soyuz TMA-09M U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz_TMA-09M)___ .

The torch also reached Europe's highest mountain, ___E:Mount Elbrus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Elbrus)___ , and Siberia's ___E:Lake Baikal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Baikal)___ .

The opening ceremony of the 2014 Winter Olympics was held on 7 February 2014 at ___E:Fisht Olympic Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisht_Olympic_Stadium)___ , an indoor arena built specifically for the ceremonies.

The ceremony featured scenes based around aspects of Russian history and arts, including ___E:ballet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballet)___ , ___E:classical music U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_music)___ , the ___E:Russian Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Revolution)___ , and the age of the ___E:Soviet Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union)___ .

The opening scene of the ceremony featured a notable technical error, where one of five snowflakes, which were to expand to form the Olympic rings, malfunctioned and did not expand (a mishap mocked by the organisers at the closing ceremony where one of the roundrelay dance groups symbolising the Olympic rings "failed" to expand).

The torch was taken into the stadium by ___E:Maria Sharapova U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Sharapova)___ , who then passed it to ___E:Yelena Isinbayeva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yelena_Isinbayeva)___ who, in turn, passed it to wrestler ___E:Aleksandr Karelin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandr_Karelin)___ .
Karelin then passed the torch to gymnast ___E:Alina Kabaeva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alina_Kabaeva)___ .

Figure skater ___E:Irina Rodnina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irina_Rodnina)___ took the torch and was met by former ice hockey goalkeeper ___E:Vladislav Tretiak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislav_Tretiak)___ , who exited the stadium to jointly light the Olympic cauldron located near the centre of Olympic Park.
A record 88 nations qualified to compete,  which beat the previous record of 82 set at the ___E:previous Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics)___ in Vancouver.
The number of athletes who qualified per country is listed in the table below (number of athletes shown in parentheses).

Seven nations made their Winter Olympics debut: ___E:Dominica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica)___ , ___E:Malta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta)___ , ___E:Paraguay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay)___ , ___E:Timor-Leste U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Timor)___ , ___E:Togo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Togo)___ , ___E:Tonga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonga)___ , and ___E:Zimbabwe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe)___ .

Meanwhile, the ___E:Philippines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines)___ returned to the Winter games after a 22-year absence, and ___E:Thailand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thailand)___ , ___E:Virgin Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Islands)___ , ___E:Luxembourg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg)___ and ___E:Venezuela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela)___ returned after 8 years.

The Winter debut of Malta meant that for the first time ever, all of the current members of the ___E:European Olympic Committees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Olympic_Committees)___ participated at the Winter Olympics.

Kristina Krone qualified to compete in her second consecutive games for ___E:Puerto Rico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico)___ , but the island's ___E:Olympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico_Olympic_Committee)___ once again chose not to send her to compete.

Similarly, ___E:South Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SASCOC)___ decided not to send alpine skier ___E:Sive Speelman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sive_Speelman&action=edit&redlink=1)___ to Sochi.
Algeria also did not enter its only qualified athlete, ___E:Mehdi-Selim Khelifi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehdi-Selim_Khelifi)___ .

___E:India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India)___ 's athletes originally competed as ___E:Independent Olympic Participants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_at_the_2014_Winter_Olympics)___ and marched under the ___E:Olympic flag U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flag)___ during the opening ceremony, as India was originally suspended in December 2012 over the election process of the ___E:Indian Olympic Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Olympic_Association)___ .
On 11 February, the Indian Olympic Association was reinstated and India's athletes were allowed the option to compete under their own flag from that time onward.
Although Shiva Keshavan competed as an Independent athlete and is recorded as such, he was permitted to walk under the flag of India at the Closing Ceremony.
During the Games some countries had a national house, a meeting place for supporters, athletes and other followers.
Houses could be either free for visitors to access or have limited access by invitation only.
The 2014 Winter Olympics featured 98 events over 15 disciplines in 7 sports.
A total of twelve new events were contested, making it the largest Winter Olympics to date.
Numbers in parentheses indicate the number of medal events contested in each separate discipline.
On 6 April 2011, the IOC accepted a number of events that were submitted by their respective sports federations to be considered for inclusion into the official program of these Olympic Games.
The events included a Figure skating team event, Women's ski jumping, Mixed relay biathlon, Ski ___E:half-pipe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-pipe)___ , and Team relay luge.
On 4 July 2011, the IOC announced that three events would be added to the program.

These events, which were officially declared by Olympic Committee President ___E:Jacques Rogge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Rogge)___ on 4 July 2011, were: Ski ___E:slopestyle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slopestyle)___ , Snowboard slopestyle, Snowboard parallel special slalom.
Team alpine skiing was also presented as a candidate for inclusion in the Olympic program but the executive board of the IOC rejected this proposal.
The ___E:International Ski Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Ski_Federation)___ persisted with the nomination and this was considered.
There were reports of ___E:bandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandy)___ possibly being added to the sports program,    but the IOC rejected this request.

Subsequently, the international governing body, ___E:Federation of International Bandy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_International_Bandy)___ , decided that ___E:Irkutsk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irkutsk)___ and ___E:Shelekhov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelekhov)___ in Russia would host the ___E:2014 Bandy World Championship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Bandy_World_Championship)___ just before the Olympics.

On 28 November 2006, the executive board of the IOC decided not to include ___E:ski mountaineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ski_mountaineering)___ ,  ___E:ski-orienteering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ski-orienteering)___ ,  or ___E:winter triathlon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_triathlon)___  in the review process of the program.

The closing ceremony was held on 23 February 2014 between 20:14 ___E:MSK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Time)___ ( ___E:UTC+4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%2B04:00)___ ) and 22:25 ___E:MSK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Time)___ ( ___E:UTC+4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC%2B04:00)___ ) at the ___E:Fisht Olympic Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisht_Olympic_Stadium)___ in ___E:Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi)___ .

The ceremony was dedicated to Russian culture featuring world-renowned Russian stars like conductor and violinist ___E:Yuri Bashmet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Bashmet)___ , conductor ___E:Valery Gergiev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valery_Gergiev)___ , pianist ___E:Denis Matsuev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Matsuev)___ , singer ___E:Hibla Gerzmava U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hibla_Gerzmava)___ and violinist Tatiana Samouil.
These artists were joined by performers from the ___E:Bolshoi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolshoi_Theatre)___ and ___E:Mariinsky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariinsky_Theatre)___ theaters.

Sochi's medal design was unveiled in May 2013. The design is intended to resemble Sochi's landscape, with a semi-translucent section containing a " ___E:patchwork quilt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patchwork_quilt)___ " of diamonds representing mountains; the diamonds themselves contain designs that reflect Russia's regions.

Those who won gold medals on 15 February received special medals with fragments of the ___E:Chelyabinsk meteor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelyabinsk_meteor)___ , marking the one-year anniversary of the event where pieces of the cosmic body fell into the ___E:Chebarkul Lake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Chebarkul)___ in the ___E:Ural Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ural_Mountains)___ in central Russia.

Security during both the Olympics and Paralympics were handled by over 40,000 ___E:law enforcement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Russia)___ officials, including ___E:police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_of_Russia)___ and the ___E:Russian Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Armed_Forces)___ .

A ___E:presidential decree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decree_of_the_President_of_Russia)___ signed by ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Russia)___ ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___ took effect on 7 January, requiring that any protests and demonstrations in Sochi and the surrounding area through 21 March (the end of the ___E:Paralympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Paralympics)___ ) be approved by the ___E:Federal Security Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Security_Service)___ .

For the duration of the decree, travel restrictions were also in effect in and around Sochi: "controlled" zones, dubbed the "ring of steel" by the media, covered the Coastal and Mountain clusters which encompass all of the Games' venues and infrastructure, including ___E:transport hubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_hub)___ such as railway stations.

To enter controlled areas, visitors were required to pass through ___E:security checkpoints U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_checkpoint)___ with ___E:X-ray machines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-ray_machine)___ , ___E:metal detectors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_detector)___ and explosive material scanners.

Several areas were designated as "forbidden", including ___E:Sochi National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_National_Park)___ and the border with ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abkhazia)___ .

An ___E:unmanned aerial vehicle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle)___ squadron, along with ___E:S-400 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S-400_Triumf)___ and ___E:Pantsir-S1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantsir-S1)___ ___E:air defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare)___ ___E:rockets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket)___ were used to protect Olympic ___E:airspace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airspace)___ .
Four ___E:gunboats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunboat)___ were also deployed on the Black Sea to protect the coastline.

A number of security organisations and forces began stationing in and around Sochi in January 2014; Russia's ___E:Ministry of Emergency Situations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Emergency_Situations_(Russia))___ (EMERCOM) was stationed in Sochi for the Games beginning on 7 January 2014.   A group of 10,000 ___E:Internal Troops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Troops_of_Russia)___ of the ___E:Ministry of Interior U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Russia))___ also provided security services during the Games.
In mid-January, 1,500 Siberian Regional Command troops were stationed in a military town near Krasnaya Polyana.
A group of 400 ___E:Cossacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cossack)___ in traditional uniforms were also present to accompany police patrols.

The ___E:58th Army unit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/58th_Army_(Russia))___ of the ___E:Russian Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Armed_Forces)___ were defending the ___E:Georgia–Russia border U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia%E2%80%93Russia_border)___ .
The United States also supplied ___E:Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ ships and other assets for security purposes.

All communication and Internet traffic by Sochi residents was captured and filtered through ___E:deep packet inspection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_packet_inspection)___ systems at all mobile networks using the ___E:SORM U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SORM)___ system.

Former professional speed skater and current deputy of the ___E:Russian State Duma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Duma)___ ___E:Svetlana Zhurova U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svetlana_Zhurova)___ has stated that the 2014 Sochi Olympics were ___E:Vladimir Putin's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___ personal project to showcase Russia to the world.
Organisers received several threats prior to the Games.

In a July 2013 video release, ___E:Chechen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chechen_people)___ ___E:Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamism)___ commander ___E:Dokka Umarov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dokka_Umarov)___ called for attacks on the Games, stating that the Games were being staged " ___E:on the bones of many, many Muslims killed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_cleansing_of_Circassians)___ ... and buried on our lands extending to the Red Sea".

Threats were received from the group ___E:Vilayat Dagestan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilayat_Dagestan)___ , which had claimed responsibility for the ___E:Volgograd bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volgograd_bombings)___ under the demands of Umarov, and a number of National Olympic Committees had also received threats via e-mail, threatening that terrorists would kidnap or "blow up" athletes during the Games.

However, while the IOC did state that the letters "[contained] no threat and appears to be a random message from a member of the public", the U.S. ski and snowboarding teams hired a private security agency to provide additional protection during the Games.

In most regions, broadcast rights to the 2014 Winter Olympics were packaged together with broadcast rights for the 2016 Summer Olympics, but some broadcasters obtained rights to further games as well. Domestic broadcast rights were sold by ___E:Sportfive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportfive)___ to a consortium of three Russian broadcasters: ___E:Channel One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_One_(Russia))___ , ___E:VGTRK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-Russia_State_Television_and_Radio_Broadcasting_Company)___ , and ___E:NTV Plus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTV_Plus)___ .

In the United States, the 2014 Winter Olympics were the first in a new, US$4.38 billion contract with ___E:NBCUniversal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBCUniversal)___ , extending its broadcast rights to the Olympic Games through 2020.

In Canada, after losing the 2010 and 2012 Games to ___E:Bell Media U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_Media)___ and ___E:Rogers Media U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Media)___ , the ___E:Canadian Broadcasting Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Broadcasting_Corporation)___ re-gained broadcast rights to the Olympics for the first time since 2008, gaining rights to the 2014 and 2016 Games.

Bell and Rogers sub-licensed pay-TV rights for their ___E:TSN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sports_Network)___ , ___E:Sportsnet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsnet)___ and ___E:Réseau des sports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9seau_des_sports)___ networks, as well as ___E:TVA Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVA_Group)___ 's ___E:TVA Sports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TVA_Sports)___ .

In Australia, after all three major commercial networks pulled out of bidding on rights to both the 2014 and 2016 Games due to cost concerns, the IOC awarded broadcast rights to just the 2014 Winter Olympics to ___E:Network Ten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_Ten)___ for A$20 million.
Several broadcasters used the Games to trial the emerging ___E:ultra high definition television U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultra_high_definition_television)___ (UHDTV) standard.

Both ___E:NTV Plus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTV_Plus)___ and ___E:Comcast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comcast)___ filmed portions of the Games in ___E:4K resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4K_resolution)___ ; Comcast offered its content through ___E:smart TV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_TV)___ apps, while NTV+ held public and cinema viewings of the content. ___E:NHK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHK)___ filmed portions of the Games in ___E:8K resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8K_resolution)___ for public viewing.
Olympic sponsor ___E:Panasonic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panasonic)___ filmed the opening ceremony in 4K.
A variety of concerns over the Games, or Russia's hosting of the Games, had been expressed by various entities.

Concerns were shown over Russia's ___E:policies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Russia)___ surrounding the ___E:LGBT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT)___ community, including the government's denial of a proposed ___E:Pride House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride_House)___ for the Games on moral grounds, and a ___E:federal law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_gay_propaganda_law)___ passed in June 2013 which criminalised the distribution of "propaganda of non-traditional sexual relationships" among minors.

Severe cost overruns made the 2014 Winter Olympics the most expensive Olympics in history, with Russian politician ___E:Boris Nemtsov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Nemtsov)___ citing allegations of corruption among government officials,  and Allison Stewart of the ___E:Saïd Business School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Business_School)___ at the ___E:University of Oxford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford)___ citing tight relationships between the government and construction firms.

It was reported that Putin's ___E:annexation of Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation)___ may have been intended to distract local Russians from corruption stories related to the Games.

U.S. broadcaster ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC)___ largely avoided broadcasting material critical of Russia, although several segments deemed "overly friendly to Russia" were criticised by some commentators.
Following the ___E:closing ceremony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics_closing_ceremony)___ , commentators evaluated the Games to have been successful overall.

Some ___E:Circassian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ organisations objected to the Games being held on land their ancestors held until 1864,   when most of them were displaced at the end of the ___E:Russian-Circassian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian-Circassian_War)___ (1763–1864), in the ___E:Circassian genocide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassian_genocide)___ .

The use of Krasnaya Polyana ("Red Hill" or "Red Glade") as an event site was considered insensitive, as it was named for a group of Circassians who were defeated in a bloody battle with Russians while attempting to return home over it in 1864.   Some Circassian groups demanded that the Games be cancelled or moved unless Russia apologised for their actions.

Other groups did not outright object to the Games, but suggested that symbols of Circassian history and culture be incorporated into the Games, as Australia, the United States and Canada did for their indigenous cultures in ___E:2000 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics)___ , ___E:2002 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics)___ , and ___E:2010 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Winter_Olympics)___ respectively.

Following the Games, reports began to emerge that the Russian Olympic team had participated in a state-run ___E:doping program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doping_in_Russia)___ , which supplied their athletes with ___E:performance-enhancing drugs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance-enhancing_drugs)___ .

These allegations first emerged in a December 2014 documentary by German public broadcaster ___E:ARD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARD_(broadcaster))___ ,  and were detailed further in a May 2016 report by The New York Times —which published allegations by Dr. ___E:Grigory Rodchenkov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigory_Rodchenkov)___ , the former director of Russia's anti-doping laboratory.

Rodchenkov alleged that a conspiracy of corrupt anti-doping officials, ___E:FSB U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Security_Service)___ intelligence agents, and compliant Russian athletes used banned substances to gain an unfair advantage during the Games.

Rodchenkov stated that the FSB tampered with over 100 urine samples as part of a ___E:cover-up U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover-up)___ , and that at least fifteen of the Russian medals won in Sochi were the result of doping.

The ___E:World Anti-Doping Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Anti-Doping_Agency)___ (WADA) commissioned an ___E:independent report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Report)___ by ___E:Richard McLaren U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_McLaren_(academic))___ , which corroborated claims that Russian authorities had been discreetly swapping out urine samples that tested positive for performance-enhancing substances.
The report concluded that the program had been operating from "at least late 2011 to August 2015", and had covered up 643 positive samples across Olympic and non-Olympic sports.

As a result, WADA considered the ___E:Russian Anti-Doping Agency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Anti-Doping_Agency)___ to be non-compliant with the World Anti-Doping Code, and recommended that Russia be banned from competing in the ___E:2016 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics)___ .

Russia was not banned from the 2016 Olympics by the IOC, a decision that was widely criticised by both athletes    and writers;    the IOC only required Russia's athletes to be cleared by an internal panel and their respective sports federations.

The ___E:IAAF U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF)___ had suspended Russia from international track and field events due to the scandal, but did allow ___E:Darya Klishina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darya_Klishina)___ to participate in the Olympics because she was confirmed not to be a part of a doping program, despite claims that surfaced in her appeal that a sample of Klishina's that had been collected on 26 February 2014 had yielded an illegal testosterone/epitestosterone ratio of 8.5 had been subject to a "SAVE" order by the Ministry of Sport on 3 March 2014.    The ___E:International Paralympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Paralympic_Committee)___ suspended the ___E:Russian Paralympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Paralympic_Committee)___ and banned the team from the ___E:2016 Summer Paralympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Paralympics)___ .

On 5 December 2017, the IOC voted to suspend the Russian Olympic Committee, thus banning it from sending athletes under the Russian flag to the ___E:2018 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Winter_Olympics)___ .
Cleared Russian athletes were allowed to participate as " ___E:Olympic Athletes from Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Athletes_from_Russia_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics)___ " (OAR).

Two of them – curler ___E:Alexander Krushelnitskiy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Krushelnitskiy)___ , who won a bronze medal, and bobsledder ___E:Nadezhda Sergeeva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadezhda_Sergeeva)___ – failed drug tests during the Games.
The IOC's ___E:Oswald Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswald_Commission)___ disqualified and banned 43 Russian athletes, and stripped thirteen medals they earned in Sochi.
In December 2017, 42 of the 43 punished athletes appealed to the ___E:Court of Arbitration for Sport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Arbitration_for_Sport)___ (CAS).
On 1 February 2018, the CAS found that the IOC provided insufficient evidence and cleared 28 athletes from IOC sanctions.
In total, Russian athletes won back 9 of the 13 medals collected.
For 11 other athletes, the CAS decided that there was sufficient evidence to uphold their Sochi sanctions, but reduced their lifetime bans to only the 2018 Winter Olympics.
The IOC said in a statement that "the result of the CAS decision does not mean that athletes from the group of 28 will be invited to the [2018 Winter Olympic] Games.
Not being sanctioned does not automatically confer the privilege of an invitation" and that "this [case] may have a serious impact on the future fight against doping".

The IOC found it important to note that the CAS Secretary General "insisted that the CAS decision does not mean that these 28 athletes are innocent” and that they would consider an appeal against the court's decision.

Later that month, the Russian Olympic Committee was reinstated by the IOC, despite failed doping tests during the 2018 Olympics,  and the Russian Anti-Doping Agency was re-certified in September, despite the Russian officials not accepting the McLaren report.

Just 4 days after the closing of the Games, Russian troops entered Ukrainian ___E:Crimea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimea)___ and started the formal ___E:annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation_of_Crimea_by_the_Russian_Federation)___ .

Russia formally incorporated Crimea into its territory on 14 March 2014.   This marked the second of three times ( ___E:2008 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Georgian_War)___ , 2014, and ___E:2022 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ ) that ___E:Russia under Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_under_Vladimir_Putin)___ invaded a neighbouring country during or immediately after the Olympic games.
